verbalization: The visible evidence suggests a potential relationship between lipoic acid and Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, mediated through UDP-glucuronosyltransferases. Lipoic acid is known to interact with UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 2B15 and 2B10, which are enzymes involved in the conjugation of endogenous and exogenous compounds. These enzymes are targets of specific compounds, including 9-Isovaleroxy Balanophonin, which in turn targets Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The shared pathway indicates that lipoic acid may influence the activity of these transporters through its interaction with UDP-glucuronosyltransferases, potentially affecting the transport of substrates across cellular membranes. The evidence is consistent across two distinct pathways, suggesting a possible mechanism by which lipoic acid modulates the function of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The strength of the evidence is supported by multiple high-scoring pathways, but the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
